Definition: from G2115; to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully:--be of good cheer (merry).
BiblicalUsage: euthyméō means be of good cheer (merry). In Acts 27:22, the text says "And now I exhort you to be of good cheer." In Acts 27:25, the text says "be of good cheer."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, euthyméō is a reminder that God's Word means what it says, and this word is part of how He speaks plainly to us. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
